requirements.requirement: Establish PostgreSQL streaming replication with node1 as writable primary and node2/node3 as standbys
requirements.summary: node1 configured with replication role, listen_addresses, wal_level=hot_standby, pg_hba entries; node2 and node3 bootstrapped via pg_basebackup -R and started as standbys. pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both node2 and node3 streaming (cmd-ef5fd1175e1f466e), and pg_is_in_recovery=true confirmed independently on both standbys (cmd-ec8f6b7dec6a4c31, cmd-f57f315a8e0c4a54).

requirements.requirement: Writes on the primary replicate to both standbys
requirements.summary: Baseline rows inserted on node1 (cmd-406c514b80644f3b) appear identically on node2 (cmd-e53466d312574c7a) and node3 (cmd-3e5f3da3976d456c) after a short propagation delay.

requirements.requirement: On loss of primary, a standby takes over as writable primary without losing committed data
requirements.summary: Pre-failover WAL LSN on node1 (0/40208E4) matched node2's received/replayed LSN (cmd-a24bbddafe8a4a0f, cmd-daff52459b8d4ada) before node1 was stopped (cmd-c2f09753e5e44a54). node2 was then promoted (cmd-11faee9142c1444c, pg_is_in_recovery=false) and accepted a new write (cmd-2028a209873c4308) while all pre-failover rows (1-3) remained intact, directly demonstrating a bounded disruption with no data loss across the transition.

requirements.requirement: Surviving standby (node3) continues/rejoins replication from the new primary
requirements.summary: An initial repoint attempt to node2 without a timeline directive stalled (cmd-4bfdb8c285434c61, cmd-52c248c58fe04432, log evidence in cmd-98f56bececdc4bfe showed timeline mismatch), but was corrected by adding recovery_target_timeline='latest' (cmd-03bbcfa128074dfc), after which node3 streamed successfully and showed all 4 rows including the post-failover write.

requirements.requirement: Recovered former primary (node1) rejoins as a standby of whichever node is now primary
requirements.summary: node1 was rebuilt via pg_basebackup against node2 with recovery_target_timeline='latest' (cmd-b969ade4c16e4eb9, cmd-5ae38ba63c01420d), came up in recovery mode with all 4 rows present, and node2's pg_stat_replication confirms both node1 and node3 streaming with node2 not in recovery (cmd-75526d8dd84d43c7).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node with pre/post boot identity, restart acknowledgement, and recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: All three nodes show pre-restart boot id and baseline data (cmd-6ae5a515989f43c8, cmd-fe7c072f1a5745df, cmd-22e7e92b00cc462e), a reboot acknowledgement (cmd-574eeb090fd54705, cmd-bfd4ee6db53545e0, cmd-5b15fa48135b4e94), a changed post-restart boot id (cmd-141145bd983840d0, cmd-20fc14f0b7134f8c, cmd-9152a570b90549e9) matching the fixed lifecycle before-prepare/after-executor boot-identity cross-check, and recovered service/data state (cmd-7992c5688c8245ba, cmd-bf52dae928984500, cmd-87284bb7b958420e). Restart order (standbys first, primary last) preserved quorum, and node2 accepted a new write and both standbys re-streamed and matched row counts afterward (cmd-d5e0bfadd87c4947, cmd-9e35519fed37427c, cmd-3e1846b75f6043f9).

overall_summary: The executor established genuine PostgreSQL 9.5 streaming replication (node1 primary, node2/node3 standbys), demonstrated a real failover with a pre/post WAL LSN check proving zero data loss, repointed the surviving standby and rebuilt the former primary as a standby of the new primary, and executed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol on all three nodes with distinct pre/post boot IDs and confirmed data/cluster recovery matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Two minor missteps (an invalid wal_level value and a missing timeline directive on node3's first repoint) were diagnosed and corrected in-band with no lasting effect.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare stage was disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state cannot be distinguished beyond the fixed before/after-executor comparison.
Password material for the replicator role is redacted in logs, so credential handling could not be independently verified beyond confirming a root-only file permission (chmod 600).
Bounded/tail-truncated log excerpts (e.g., cmd-98f56bececdc4bfe) were relied on for diagnosing the node3 timeline issue; full log context was not available.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all state-changing commands in order. Package installs, config edits, pg_basebackup rebuilds, promotion, and reboots each map directly to a material outcome or a necessary prerequisite/correction. Two self-corrected missteps are notable but low-risk and fully remediated: (1) cmd-c2a96094fc2e4978 set wal_level=replica, an invalid value for PostgreSQL 9.5, immediately fixed by cmd-1cc1c10d1dee459e before any dependent state was built on it; (2) node3's first recovery.conf repoint (cmd-4bfdb8c285434c61) lacked a timeline directive causing a stalled/looping replication attempt, diagnosed via cmd-98f56bececdc4bfe and corrected by cmd-03bbcfa128074dfc, bounded, low-risk, and fully resolved with no residue. The demonstration table 'ft' was left in the databases, but it is core to proving replication/failover behavior rather than unrelated residue. No failed services, unsafe exposure, or damaged package state observed after_executor.
